hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي مَالِك أَنَّهُ بَلَغَهُ ، عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ الْأَنْصَارِيِّ وَكَانَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنْ الرَّجُلِ تَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ رَقَبَةٌ ، هَلْ يَجُوزُ لَهُ أَنْ يُعْتِقَ وَلَدَ زِنًا ؟ قَالَ : نَعَمْ ، ذَلِكَ يُجْزِئُ عَنْهُ

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated that Abdullah ibn Umar was asked about an obligatory manumission, whether it may be purchased with a condition. He said: 'No.' Malik said: 'This is the best of what I have heard concerning obligatory manumissions: that the one who frees should not purchase the slave that he will free for what is obligatory upon him with a condition that he will free them, because if he does that, it is not a complete manumission, as he reduces from their price for the one who stipulates their freedom.' Malik said: 'There is no harm in purchasing a slave for voluntary manumission and stipulating that he will free them.' Malik said: 'The best of what has been heard concerning obligatory manumissions is that it is not permissible to free therein a Christian or a Jew, nor to free therein a mukatab (contracted slave), mudabbar (posthumously freed slave), umm walad (mother of a child), one freed to a set time, or a blind person. There is no harm in freeing a Christian, Jew, or Magian voluntarily, because Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said in His Book: "Either favor afterwards or ransom" (Surah Muhammad, verse 4), and the favor is manumission.' Malik said: 'As for the obligatory manumissions that Allah mentioned in the Book, none should be freed therein except a believing slave.' Malik said: 'Likewise in feeding the poor in expiations, none should be fed therein except Muslims, and none on other than the religion of Islam should be fed therein.'

hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنِي مَالِك أَنَّهُ بَلَغَهُ ، أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عُمَرَ ، سُئِلَ عَنْ الرَّقَبَةِ الْوَاجِبَةِ ، هَلْ تُشْتَرَى بِشَرْطٍ ؟ فَقَالَ : لَا . قَالَ مَالِك : وَذَلِكَ أَحْسَنُ مَا سَمِعْتُ فِي الرِّقَابِ الْوَاجِبَةِ ، أَنَّهُ لَا يَشْتَرِيهَا الَّذِي يُعْتِقُهَا فِيمَا وَجَبَ عَلَيْهِ بِشَرْطٍ عَلَى أَنْ يُعْتِقَهَا ، لِأَنَّهُ إِذَا فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ فَلَيْسَتْ بِرَقَبَةٍ تَامَّةٍ ، لِأَنَّهُ يَضَعُ مِنْ ثَمَنِهَا لِلَّذِي يَشْتَرِطُ مِنْ عِتْقِهَا . قَالَ مَالِك : وَلَا بَأْسَ أَنْ يَشْتَرِيَ الرَّقَبَةَ فِي التَّطَوُّعِ ، وَيَشْتَرِطَ أَنْ يُعْتِقَهَا . قَالَ مَالِك : إِنَّ أَحْسَنَ مَا سُمِعَ فِي الرِّقَابِ الْوَاجِبَةِ ، أَنَّهُ لَا يَجُوزُ أَنْ يُعْتَقَ فِيهَا نَصْرَانِيٌّ وَلَا يَهُودِيٌّ ، وَلَا يُعْتَقُ فِيهَا مُكَاتَبٌ وَلَا مُدَبَّرٌ ، وَلَا أُمُّ وَلَدٍ وَلَا مُعْتَقٌ إِلَى سِنِينَ وَلَا أَعْمَى ، وَلَا بَأْسَ أَنْ يُعْتَقَ النَّصْرَانِيُّ وَالْيَهُودِيُّ وَالْمَجُوسِيُّ تَطَوُّعًا ، لِأَنَّ اللَّهَ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى ، قَالَ فِي كِتَابِهِ : فَإِمَّا مَنًّا بَعْدُ وَإِمَّا فِدَاءً سورة محمد آية 4 ، فَالْمَنُّ : الْعَتَاقَةُ . قَالَ مَالِك : فَأَمَّا الرِّقَابُ الْوَاجِبَةُ الَّتِي ذَكَرَ اللَّهُ فِي الْكِتَابِ ، فَإِنَّهُ لَا يُعْتَقُ فِيهَا إِلَّا رَقَبَةٌ مُؤْمِنَةٌ . قَالَ مَالِك : وَكَذَلِكَ فِي إِطْعَامِ الْمَسَاكِينِ فِي الْكَفَّارَاتِ ، لَا يَنْبَغِي أَنْ يُطْعَمَ فِيهَا إِلَّا الْمُسْلِمُونَ ، وَلَا يُطْعَمُ فِيهَا أَحَدٌ عَلَى غَيْرِ دِينِ الْإِسْلَامِ

hadiths.english_translation:
First narration: Narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Amrah al-Ansari that his mother intended to make a bequest, then she delayed it until morning, and she died. She had intended to free a slave. Abd al-Rahman said: 'So I said to al-Qasim ibn Muhammad: Will it benefit her if I free a slave on her behalf?' Al-Qasim said: 'Sa'd ibn Ubadah said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "My mother has died, will it benefit her if I free a slave on her behalf?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Yes."'

Second narration: Narrated from Yahya ibn Sa'id that he said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr died in a sleep he was sleeping, so Aisha, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, freed many slaves on his behalf.' Malik said: 'This is the most beloved of what I have heard to me concerning that.'

hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنِي مَالِك ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَمْرَةَ الْأَنْصَارِيِّ ، أَنَّ أُمَّهُ أَرَادَتْ أَنْ تُوصِيَ ، ثُمَّ أَخَّرَتْ ذَلِكَ إِلَى أَنْ تُصْبِحَ ، فَهَلَكَتْ ، وَقَدْ كَانَتْ هَمَّتْ بِأَنْ تُعْتِقَ ، فَقَالَ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ : فَقُلْتُ لِلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ : أَيَنْفَعُهَا أَنْ أُعْتِقَ عَنْهَا ؟ فَقَالَ الْقَاسِمُ : إِنَّ سَعْدَ بْنَ عُبَادَةَ قَالَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ إِنَّ أُمِّي هَلَكَتْ ، فَهَلْ يَنْفَعُهَا أَنْ أُعْتِقَ عَنْهَا ؟ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : نَعَمْ . وَحَدَّثَنِي مَالِك ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ سَعِيدٍ ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ : تُوُفِّيَ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ فِي نَوْمٍ نَامَهُ ، فَأَعْتَقَتْ عَنْهُ عَائِشَةُ زَوْجُ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ رِقَابًا كَثِيرَةً . قَالَ مَالِك : وَهَذَا أَحَبُّ مَا سَمِعْتُ إِلَيَّ فِي ذَلِكَ

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Aisha, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, that she said: Barira came and said: 'I have made a contract with my people for nine uqiyyahs, one uqiyyah per year, so help me.' Aisha said: 'If your people would like me to count it out for them on your behalf, I will count it, and your walaa (clientage) will be mine, I will do so.' So Barira went to her people and told them that, but they refused. She came back from her people while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting. She said to Aisha: 'I offered them that, but they refused unless the walaa would be theirs.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard that and asked her, so Aisha informed him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Take her and stipulate the walaa for them, for walaa belongs only to the one who frees.' So Aisha did that. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood before the people, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'To proceed: What is the matter with men who stipulate conditions not in the Book of Allah? Whatever condition is not in the Book of Allah is invalid, even if it be a hundred conditions. The decree of Allah is more deserving, and the condition of Allah is more binding. Walaa belongs only to the one who frees.'

hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنِي مَالِك ، عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ زَوْجِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، أَنَّهَا قَالَتْ : جَاءَتْ بَرِيرَةُ ، فَقَالَتْ : إِنِّي كَاتَبْتُ أَهْلِي عَلَى تِسْعِ أَوَاقٍ فِي كُلِّ عَامٍ أُوقِيَّةٌ ، فَأَعِينِينِي . فَقَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ : إِنْ أَحَبَّ أَهْلُكِ أَنْ أَعُدَّهَا لَهُمْ عَنْكِ عَدَدْتُهَا ، وَيَكُونَ لِي وَلَاؤُكِ ، فَعَلْتُ . فَذَهَبَتْ بَرِيرَةُ إِلَى أَهْلِهَا ، فَقَالَتْ لَهُمْ ذَلِكَ ، فَأَبَوْا عَلَيْهَا ، فَجَاءَتْ مِنْ عِنْدِ أَهْلِهَا وَرَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ جَالِسٌ ، فَقَالَتْ لِعَائِشَةَ : إِنِّي قَدْ عَرَضْتُ عَلَيْهِمْ ذَلِكَ ، فَأَبَوْا عَلَيَّ إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ الْوَلَاءُ لَهُمْ ، فَسَمِعَ ذَلِكَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، فَسَأَلَهَا ، فَأَخْبَرَتْهُ عَائِشَةُ ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : خُذِيهَا وَاشْتَرِطِي لَهُمُ الْوَلَاءَ ، فَإِنَّمَا الْوَلَاءُ لِمَنْ أَعْتَقَ . فَفَعَلَتْ عَائِشَةُ ، ثُمَّ قَامَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي النَّاسِ ، فَحَمِدَ اللَّهَ وَأَثْنَى عَلَيْهِ ، ثُمَّ قَالَ : أَمَّا بَعْدُ فَمَا بَالُ رِجَالٍ يَشْتَرِطُونَ شُرُوطًا لَيْسَتْ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ ، مَا كَانَ مِنْ شَرْطٍ لَيْسَ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ فَهُوَ بَاطِلٌ ، وَإِنْ كَانَ مِائَةَ شَرْطٍ ، قَضَاءُ اللَّهِ أَحَقُّ ، وَشَرْطُ اللَّهِ أَوْثَقُ ، وَإِنَّمَا الْوَلَاءُ لِمَنْ أَعْتَقَ

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Nafi' from Abdullah ibn Umar that Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, wanted to purchase a slave girl to free her. Her people said: 'We will sell her to you on condition that her walaa is for us.' So she mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: 'Let not that prevent you, for walaa belongs only to the one who frees.'

hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي مَالِك ، عَنْ نَافِعٍ ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ ، أَنَّ عَائِشَةَ أُمَّ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَرَادَتْ أَنْ تَشْتَرِيَ جَارِيَةً تُعْتِقُهَا ، فَقَالَ أَهْلُهَا : نَبِيعُكِهَا عَلَى أَنَّ وَلَاءَهَا لَنَا . فَذَكَرَتْ ذَلِكَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، فَقَالَ : لَا يَمْنَعَنَّكِ ذَلِكَ فَإِنَّمَا الْوَلَاءُ لِمَنْ أَعْتَقَ

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Amrah bint Abd al-Rahman, that Barira came seeking help from Aisha, the Mother of the Believers. Aisha said: 'If your people would like me to pour out your price for them in one payment and free you, I will do so.' So Barira mentioned that to her people, and they said: 'No, unless the walaa is for us.' Yahya ibn Sa'id said: Amrah claimed that Aisha mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Purchase her and free her, for walaa belongs only to the one who frees.'

potential_issues.impact: Minor concern. The word 'za'amat' is used by reliable narrators and doesn't necessarily imply doubt, but it's less strong than direct affirmation. However, all narrators are highly reliable, and Amrah was a direct student of Aisha.

potential_issues.issue: This is another version of the Barira story, with a slightly different chain than hadith 9550.
potential_issues.impact: The existence of multiple chains strengthens the overall authenticity of the Barira incident, as it shows the story was widely transmitted through different reliable routes.

hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي مَالِك ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ سَعِيدٍ ، عَنْ عَمْرَةَ بِنْتِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ ، أَنَّ بَرِيرَةَ جَاءَتْ تَسْتَعِينُ عَائِشَةَ أُمَّ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ، فَقَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ : إِنْ أَحَبَّ أَهْلُكِ أَنْ أَصُبَّ لَهُمْ ثَمَنَكِ صَبَّةً وَاحِدَةً وَأُعْتِقَكِ ، فَعَلْتُ . فَذَكَرَتْ ذَلِكَ بَرِيرَةُ لِأَهْلِهَا ، فَقَالُوا : لَا ، إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ لَنَا وَلَاؤُكِ . قَالَ يَحْيَى بْنُ سَعِيدٍ : فَزَعَمَتْ عَمْرَةُ أَنَّ عَائِشَةَ ذَكَرَتْ ذَلِكَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : اشْتَرِيهَا وَأَعْتِقِيهَا فَإِنَّمَا الْوَلَاءُ لِمَنْ أَعْتَقَ

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Abdullah ibn Dinar from Abdullah ibn Umar that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the selling of walaa and its gifting. Malik said regarding a slave who purchases himself from his master on condition that he may give his walaa to whomever he wishes: 'That is not permissible, and walaa belongs only to the one who frees. Even if a man gave permission to his freed slave to give his walaa to whomever he wishes, that would not be permissible, because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Walaa belongs to the one who frees." And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the selling of walaa and its gifting. So if it were permissible for his master to stipulate that for him and to give him permission to give walaa to whomever he wishes, that would be the gifting.'

hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي مَالِك ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ دِينَارٍ ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ ، أَنّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ نَهَى عَنْ بَيْعِ الْوَلَاءِ وَعَنْ هِبَتِهِ . قَالَ مَالِك ، فِي الْعَبْدِ يَبْتَاعُ نَفْسَهُ مِنْ سَيِّدِهِ عَلَى أَنَّهُ يُوَالِي مَنْ شَاءَ : إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَا يَجُوزُ ، وَإِنَّمَا الْوَلَاءُ لِمَنْ أَعْتَقَ ، وَلَوْ أَنَّ رَجُلًا أَذِنَ لِمَوْلَاهُ أَنْ يُوَالِيَ مَنْ شَاءَ مَا جَازَ ذَلِكَ ، لِأَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، قَالَ : الْوَلَاءُ لِمَنْ أَعْتَقَ . وَنَهَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَنْ بَيْعِ الْوَلَاءِ وَعَنْ هِبَتِهِ ، فَإِذَا جَازَ لِسَيِّدِهِ أَنْ يَشْتَرِطَ ذَلِكَ لَهُ وَأَنْ يَأْذَنَ لَهُ أَنْ يُوَالِيَ مَنْ شَاءَ ، فَتِلْكَ الْهِبَةُ
hadiths.grade: Sahih (core hadith), plus Malik's juristic reasoning

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Rabi'ah ibn Abi Abd al-Rahman that al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam purchased a slave and freed him. That slave had sons from a free woman. When al-Zubayr freed him, he said: 'They are my clients (mawali).' And the clients of their mother said: 'Rather, they are our clients.' So they disputed before Uthman ibn Affan, and Uthman ruled in favor of al-Zubayr regarding their walaa.

narrators.name: Malik
narrators.full_name: Malik ibn Anas ibn Malik ibn Abi Amir al-Asbahi

narrators.name: Rabi'ah ibn Abi Abd al-Rahman
narrators.full_name: Rabi'ah ibn Abi Abd al-Rahman Farrukh al-Madani

chainIssues: Rabi'ah is reporting about an event involving Zubayr ibn al-Awwam and Uthman ibn Affan without an intermediary
Rabi'ah was born around 60 AH, while Zubayr died in 36 AH and Uthman in 35 AH - impossible for direct witnessing
The chain is mursal/munqati' with missing intermediaries who witnessed the event

plainChains: Malik -> Rabi'ah ibn Abi Abd al-Rahman -> [Missing intermediary/witnesses] -> Incident involving Zubayr and Uthman

potential_issues.issue: Rabi'ah ibn Abi Abd al-Rahman (born c. 60 AH) is reporting about an incident involving Zubayr (died 36 AH) and Uthman (died 35 AH). There's a clear generational gap with no intermediary mentioned.
potential_issues.impact: This is a mursal or munqati' chain. At least one generation of narrators is missing between Rabi'ah and the eyewitnesses of this event, creating significant uncertainty about the reliability of the report.

potential_issues.issue: This is a mawquf narration reporting a legal ruling by the Companion Uthman, not a marfu' hadith from the Prophet ﷺ.
potential_issues.impact: While Companion rulings are valuable, they don't carry the same authority as prophetic statements. This is more of a legal precedent than hadith evidence.

potential_issues.issue: The use of 'an (عَنْ) by Rabi'ah when he couldn't have witnessed the event himself is particularly problematic.
potential_issues.impact: The ambiguous transmission term combined with the clear chronological impossibility makes this chain weak.

Topics: Walaa of children born to a slave father and free mother

Legal ruling of Uthman on inherited walaa
hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنِي مَالِك ، عَنْ رَبِيعَةَ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ ، أَنَّ الزُّبَيْرَ بْنَ الْعَوَّامِ اشْتَرَى عَبْدًا فَأَعْتَقَهُ ، وَلِذَلِكَ الْعَبْدِ بَنُونَ مِنَ امْرَأَةٍ حُرَّةٍ ، فَلَمَّا أَعْتَقَهُ الزُّبَيْرُ ، قَالَ : هُمْ مَوَالِيَّ ، وَقَالَ مَوَالِي أُمِّهِمْ : بَلْ هُمْ مَوَالِينَا . فَاخْتَصَمُوا إِلَى عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عَفَّانَ ، فَقَضَى عُثْمَانُ لِلزُّبَيْرِ بِوَلَائِهِمْ
